ranking.note: Raised to P1: release-binary verification can report success from revoked/expired keys only, a security defect in release integrity tooling, on par with the other P1 release-integrity bug.
Raised to P2 and moved up: it is the direct prerequisite for the P2 Qt 6.12 update (#36593) and cannot sit below it.
Raised to P2 for parity with the GCC 13 bump (#36042): both are the same compiler-baseline transition and both gate the C++23 RFC.
Placed after its two prerequisite compiler-baseline bumps, which must be decided first; it is an explicit WIP/RFC on top of them.
Moved up: it fixes real configure-time feature misdetection under -Werror and is cited as unblocking the P2 clang-cl migration (#31507).
Moved up slightly: the upstream URL 404s today, so depends currently depends solely on the fallback mirror.
Moved up: it fixes an actual failure for release signers running codesigning in containers, which is release tooling breakage rather than cosmetics.
Moved up: local port hijacking of the P2P listener is a security problem for Windows node operators, ranked above pure build hygiene.
Moved down: a build-structure refactor with no cited breakage or blocked PR ranks below concrete build/platform failures, though its kernel-library payoff keeps it high in P3.
Moved down: BSD is not a release platform and reviewers are still disputing whether all three BSDs belong on every PR, so the benefit is less certain than the macOS/Guix CI work above.
Moved down: CI hermeticity is preventive and no concrete leak-caused failure is cited, so it ranks below CI work tied to observed breakage.
Moved up: dropping a compiled Boost library from CMake, depends, Guix and vcpkg removes a recurring packaging burden, the strongest payoff among the maintainability items.
Moved up: removing privileged container execution from CI and the BCC/root requirement is a tangible CI and contributor-friction win, not a cosmetic cleanup.
Moved up: unlike the other warning-flag PRs it cites a real bug class (#36137) the flag would have caught.
Moved down: packaging convenience with a clear use case but no breakage; ranks below build/CI items tied to observed failures.
Moved down: scaffolding for a future online-wallet feature that itself depends on two unmerged PRs, so present value is speculative.
Moved down: a maintainer-workflow convenience whose value is real but unproven, below CI changes that protect correctness of the build.
Moved down: narrow Windows path-quoting coverage whose first finding is a test-harness bug, not a product defect.
Moved down: a few-percent binary size saving is grouped with the other size-reduction PRs, below functional build and CI fixes.
Moved down: affects only builds against an external/CI libmultiprocess, not any in-tree default build.
Moved down: configure-time guard for an optional, experimental IPC build path on unusual system capnproto setups.
Lowered to P4: the card states repository defaults already enforce read-only tokens, so the problem is largely already mitigated.
Lowered to P4 and moved down: the author confirms no CI failures have actually been observed, an alternate approach was proposed, and the whole BSD cross-CI path may be replaced by #36147.

inconsistencies: Chain: #36592 (macOS SDK 15) is a hard prerequisite for #36593 (Qt 6.12). Review #36592 first; it was originally banded below the PR it unblocks.
Chain: #36036 (clang 19) and #36042 (GCC 13) are exactly the baselines #36033 (C++23 RFC) requires. Decide the two bumps first; the RFC is only actionable after them.
#36554 is cited as unblocking native clang-cl compilation tracked in #31507; the prerequisite should be reviewed ahead of or alongside the P2 migration.

Overlapping goal: #36534 (hardening flags for the secp256k1 subtree) and #36649 (hardening flags for depends packages) are the same campaign by the same author. #36534 first: it fixes an observed loss of binary-wide BTI/PAC/GCS markers, whereas #36649 is defence in depth.

Four global warning-flag PRs will conflict with each other and all touch the same CMake block: #36167 (-Wunused), #35911 (-Wmissing-noreturn), #36268 (-Wextra-semi), #36623 (-Wunreachable-code-aggressive). Review in that order; the latter two also wait on subtree updates.

Overlapping area: #36147 replaces BSD cross-compile CI tasks with native VM jobs, which would make #35722 (caching BSD SDK downloads for the cross tasks) largely moot. Settle #36147's direction first.

Overlapping scope: #35774 (native testing of cross-built macOS arm64 binaries) and #36082 (full Guix build-and-test workflow in CI) both aim to test release-like artifacts before release; coordinate so the macOS job is not implemented twice.

Both #28690 (adds dependency rules to check-deps.sh) and #35167 (rewrites check-deps.sh in Python, driven by doc/design/libraries.md) modify the same dependency check. Whichever lands second will need rework; #28690 defines the targets the checker describes, so it should be settled first.
#36592's own assessment ranked it two bands of positions below #36593, which it blocks; that was the clearest band inversion in the list and is corrected here.
result.notes: The category splits cleanly: two release-integrity defects (wrong source tree in Guix builds, verification accepting revoked keys) sit alone at P1; a P2 group covering release-binary security, supported-platform build/run breakage, release-artifact CI coverage and the compiler/Qt baseline transitions; a broad P3 body of concrete build and CI fixes; and a P4 tail of cosmetic flags, doc and tooling bumps. Several multiprocess/IPC build PRs (#19460, #32387, #36060, #35454, #36556) are all P3 but serve a not-yet-default subsystem, so they rank below fixes affecting default builds.
